candidate.blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Management of Care; coordinate individualized plans of care, communicate treatment changes, and support continuity across settings
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — individualized school diabetes plan after treatment change
candidate.educational_objective: Coordinate safe school diabetes care by ensuring the student’s individualized DMMP is updated whenever the diabetes regimen changes and that relevant trained school personnel can follow the current monitoring, treatment, and emergency instructions.

options.A: Obtain and implement an updated individualized Diabetes Medical Management Plan (DMMP) that reflects the student’s current monitoring, insulin, hypo/hyperglycemia, and emergency-care instructions.
options.B: Continue using the prior DMMP until the next school year because diabetes plans are updated only annually.
options.C: Replace the individualized DMMP with the school’s general diabetes policy because one district-wide plan is sufficient for every student.
options.D: Keep the revised diabetes instructions only for the school nurse and avoid communicating applicable emergency procedures to trained school personnel.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current ADA school guidance states that each student with diabetes should have an individualized DMMP developed by the health care professional in collaboration with the student and parent or guardian. The DMMP is the basis for school diabetes care and emergency planning and should be updated annually or whenever the student’s regimen, self-management level, or school circumstances change. B delays a required update after a treatment change. C ignores the individualized medical orders. D is unsafe because appropriate school personnel need training and access to the instructions necessary to provide care and respond to emergencies.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Students with diabetes require an individualized DMMP that guides monitoring, treatment, and emergency care at school and should be updated when the diabetes regimen or relevant circumstances change.
candidate.source_document_title: Diabetes Care in the School Setting: A Statement of the American Diabetes Association; Diabetes Medical Management Plan; Children and Adolescents: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026
candidate.source_locator: 2024 ADA school statement, DMMP section — individualized plan addresses monitoring, insulin, hypo/hyperglycemia, emergency needs and is updated annually or whenever care changes; ADA Safe at School DMMP page — update annually or when regimen, self-management, or school circumstances change; 2026 Section 14 ‘School and Child Care’ — school personnel should provide care according to the individualized DMMP

candidate.stem: A student with type 1 diabetes returns to school after the diabetes care team changes the student’s insulin regimen and continuous glucose monitor settings. Which action by the school nurse is most appropriate?
